goal: Hook: the teacher and two volunteers play a one-minute scene from a posted outline; pose the compelling question; study commedia dell'arte, Italy 1500s and 1600s, and the plot outlines Flaminio Scala printed in 1611 that players filled with their own words (who, where, when, what for); connecting (practiced, no id claimed): what the 1611 players and the class both do with an outline.
note: Words: improvise, character, setting. Sensitivity: masks and stock types are studied in pictures only; students play a want and a walk, never an accent, a regional type or a mask of a real group. Safe use: clear floor with room for arms out, chairs and bags to the walls, bare feet or soft soles; freezes held still, no falls. Free path: chairs, a scarf, the voice.

goal: Opener retrieval with its reteach; then the freeze shown in named steps with the step card (signal, hold, breathe, release) and the what-if list taught as one way of finding ideas.
note: Retrieval (10 minutes): a "what if" detail and a made-up line (th-g2-imagine) and the group agreements card (th-g2-show), last used in grade 2 of Theater K to 2; the reteach runs as written for any student new to theater. Words: method, idea, group.

goal: Viola Spolin's "Where" game, described in our words and credited to her: a place shown only by the objects used in it; groups try it and start the idea sheet.
note: Spolin (United States, 1906 to 1994), described, never copied. The idea sheet names the method tried and the idea it gave.

goal: Warm-up, then the freeze and the "Where" game run three times in groups with feedback after each run.
note: Baseline look (rotating groups, met, partly or not yet) on the unit's main look-for: a character, a place and a story the group made up from the card, clear to the audience.

goal: The scenario-to-scene steps shown with the step card on a Curio Class scenario card (read the outline, cast, find the place, run, freeze, fix), and a group deciding how each character moves and speaks.
note: Scenario cards are Curio Class's own, in the commedia outline form.

goal: Groups improvise a scene from a new scenario card with the steps, each student choosing a role and the group agreeing on each character's walk and voice.
note: A student who does not want to perform takes the timer job or the "Where" objects and is marked on the idea sheet and log. Passed objects checked by the teacher first. Shorter path (spare fold-in day): folds into day 5, as a 15-minute segment.

goal: Comparing two ideas for a scene and keeping the one that makes it stronger, shown on a teacher-played beat; a third idea method: one object passed round and used three ways.
note: Words: compare, strengthen. The passed object is checked by the teacher (no sharp edges, nothing small enough to swallow, no cords). Shorter path (spare fold-in day): folds into day 8, as a 15-minute segment.

goal: Groups pick the scenario card for their showing and build the scene, trying two ideas and keeping one; each student adds the method and idea to the idea sheet.
Working inside a limit: the two-minute pace cue on the teacher's timer and a space taped on the floor, and the rehearsal-log page taught (what we ran, what we kept, what we change next).
note: The teacher keeps the timer as a pace cue; no student measures or counts time. Words: rehearse, limit, reflect.

goal: Warm-up, then the group scene run inside the two-minute cue and the taped space three times, with a spoken rehearsal-log check after each run.
note: Shorter path (named fold-in day, a year 10 school days short): folds into day 11, as the opener.

goal: Rehearsal with the unit's one critique, led aloud by the teacher in three steps (describe, ask, suggest), each suggestion tied to a look-for; the teacher marks look-fors on the record sheet.
note: Critique practices collaborative talk (SL.3.1, practiced, not owned); the group agreements card shows the turns.

goal: Revision: groups rework the scene from the critique and each student says in one line what the group changed.
Last rehearsal: a full run inside the limit; each student completes the rehearsal-log page (one line alone, one with the group) and the idea sheet.
note: These kept pages are scored after the written day (end-of-unit evidence for TH:Pr6.1.3a and TH:Cr2.1.3a).

goal: Showing day: each group's two-minute scenario scene for the class, marked live on the guide; each student's self-check on the same guide.
note: Look-fors: a character, a place and a story the group made up from the card, clear to the audience (Cr1.1.3a); the agreed way the student's character moves and speaks (Cr1.1.3c); the scene fits the two-minute cue and the taped space (Cr3.1.3a). Set-up 3, warm-up 5, six groups of five about 4 minutes each (24), self-check 3, close 4. A group the teacher cannot watch live is recorded on the school device that day (hands, props and sound only where the family said no to faces) and marked before the respond day. Response time: the respond day after the written day, counted once.

goal: Written day: on the teacher's unseen scene, the student picks the stronger of two ideas and says why; the rehearsal-log page and idea sheet are collected with the portfolio reflection.
note: Written day: set-up 3, the teacher performs the unseen Curio Class scene twice (6), response card (15, at most two written items; a student may answer aloud at the table, marked the same), kept cards collected and the one-line portfolio reflection (5), close 4. Items: Cr2.1.3b written; Pr6.1.3a the kept rehearsal-log page; Cr2.1.3a the kept idea sheet. Portfolio piece: the rehearsal-log page.

goal: Respond: a second try at the part marked "not yet" (a clearer character or place, a scene fitted to the cue) and a re-run before a second showing to one other group.
note: Groups from the record sheet, at most four; the rest work in pairs from the written move. Starts from marks already made; no first-time evidence is collected.

goal: Hook: the teacher walks one character three ways; pose the compelling question; study kyogen, the comic theater of Japan, from pictures and descriptions: the set walk, the big clear voice, the fan used as a door, and why an actor makes that choice; connecting (practiced, no id claimed): where kyogen sits on a day of noh and why families hand it down.
note: Kyogen from UNESCO's page and a Japanese cultural body's page; no kyogen costume, mask or Japanese voice is used, and the unit plan picks a play free of drinking and harm. Words: reason, decision. Safe use: clear floor with room for arms out, chairs and bags to the walls, bare feet or soft soles.

goal: Opener retrieval with its reteach; then the body set shown in steps with the step card (shake out, levels, a walk).
note: Retrieval (10 minutes): one character walked and spoken two ways (th-g2-actor) and an audience card on one performer's choice of voice or movement (th-g2-notice), last used in grade 2; reteach as written. No spinning past three turns.

goal: The voice set (hum, siren, a line to the back wall) and the thinking set (a memory game, the count to twenty) shown in steps with the step card.
note: Voice kept below shouting, with a rest after the siren. Words: exercise, voice, body. Shorter path (spare fold-in day): folds into day 20, as a 15-minute segment of the fluency day that runs the sets.

goal: Warm-up: the three exercise sets run as one routine three times, with feedback on each set.
note: Baseline look (rotating groups) on the main look-for: body and voice explored for a character. Arms-out space.

goal: Study Bill Irwin, a clown and actor who builds characters from the body (described and linked to a public page on his work), and the character map taught: how the character moves, speaks and thinks.
note: The unit plan records whether Irwin is living, as of its date. Words: movement, character.

goal: Exploring body and voice for a character, first in an unscripted beat and then in a two-line Curio Class script the teacher reads aloud.
note: Words: explore. The two-line script is learned by ear and by the card.

goal: Pairs choose a character, fill its character map and play it unscripted, then from the two-line script, making the two versions different.
note: Shorter path (spare fold-in day): folds into day 22, as a 15-minute segment.

goal: Connecting with a character's feelings and naming our own experiences of joining in or watching drama, on a short teacher-played scene; the response card frame taught ("I think ___ because ___. I saw it when ___.").
note: Bridge: ELA grade 3 teaches opinion writing with a reason in unit 3 (weeks 17 to 24), after this unit, so the response card gives the frame and at most two written items. Experiences need no paid show: at least one comes from this year's theater class (a class scene, a partner showing), which every student has; the second may be a show, a story told at home or an invented one, marked the same. Words: experience, connect, feeling.

goal: Warm-up sets, then the two versions of the pair's beat run three times with feedback; partners fill an audience card on one choice and its reason.
note: Shorter path (named fold-in day, a year 10 school days short): folds into day 26, as the opener.

goal: Rehearsal of both versions of the two-line scene, the character map updated with the movement and voice chosen.
Rehearsal with the unit's one critique, led by the teacher (describe, ask, suggest) and tied to the look-fors.
Revision: pairs rework one version from the critique and say in one line what changed.
Last rehearsal: both versions run; each student completes the character map with the movement and voice chosen and where a studied work showed it.
note: The kept character map is the end-of-unit evidence for TH:Pr4.1.3b, scored after the written day.

goal: Showing day: the warm-up that opens the day is marked for each of the three sets; each pair plays its two-line scene twice for the class; the audience fills an audience-journal card on another group's choice and its reason.
note: Look-fors: the student joins each of the three sets (Pr5.1.3a); body and voice explored, the two versions different (Cr3.1.3b). Kept: the audience-journal card (Re7.1.3a). A group the teacher cannot watch live is recorded on the school device that day (hands, props and sound only where the family said no to faces) and marked before the respond day. Response time: the respond day after the written day, counted once.

goal: Written day: on the unseen scene, a character's feeling and how the student connects with it, and two of the student's own experiences of drama this year; the character map is collected.
note: Written day: set-up 3, the teacher performs the unseen Curio Class scene twice (6), response card (15, at most two written items; a student may answer aloud at the table, marked the same), kept cards collected and the one-line portfolio reflection (5), close 4. Items: Re8.1.3c and Re8.1.3a written (at least one experience from this year's theater class; the second may be a show, a story told at home or an invented one, marked the same); Pr4.1.3b the kept character map. Portfolio piece: the audience-journal card.

goal: Respond: a second try at the part marked "not yet" (a set joined fully, a version made different) and a re-run of the scene for one other pair.
note: Groups from the record sheet, at most four; the rest work in pairs from the written move. Starts from marks already made; no first-time evidence is collected.

goal: Year 3 mid-year check: a fresh improvisation in groups of five from a new scenario card, marked live, and a kept card filled while another group plays on which of two ideas the student's group kept and why; items drawn from unit 1, not from unit 2 just assessed.
note: Check day: set-up 3, warm-up 3, the groups read the new card, plan and rehearse (8), each student completes the record the card names (4), six group slots of 3 minutes, each performance at most 2 minutes (18), close 4. The teacher marks one group at a time and reads the cards after the session; no artifact is scored twice. Marked live: characters, a place and a story the group made up from the card (Cr1.1.3a), the agreed walk and voice (Cr1.1.3c), the scene fitted to the two-minute cue (Cr3.1.3a); kept card: Cr2.1.3b. Unit 2's record (days 30 and 31) is carried unscored; no exercise-set task repeats. Week 17. Two-week rule (lead call 6, 2026-11-26): the check follows the unit's showing, but it is a showing on earlier-unit work from a fresh card with its own items, so no item repeats inside two weeks.

goal: Respond to the mid-year check: a second try at the part marked "not yet", in groups from the record sheet.
note: Groups from the record sheet, at most four; the rest work in pairs from the written move. Starts from marks already made; no first-time evidence is collected.

goal: Hook: a chair, a scarf and a card crown turn the room into a place; pose the compelling question; the basic tech elements of a drama named (costume, prop, set, light, sound; makeup named but not used).
note: Words: set, costume, prop, tech element. Safe use: clear floor with room for arms out, chairs and bags to the walls, bare feet or soft soles.

goal: Opener retrieval with its reteach; then a scene of L. Frank Baum's The Wonderful Wizard of Oz (1900) retold, with Denslow's first pictures as the book's background, and the labeled design sketch shown in steps: costume, prop and set ideas that suit the setting and characters.
note: Retrieval (10 minutes): a prop-sketch of one place (th-g2-design) and the two-ties card (th-g2-world), last used in grade 2; reteach as written. Words: design, decision.

goal: Study The Wiz (Broadway, 1975), the stage retelling with an all-Black cast whose costumes Geoffrey Holder (born in Trinidad) designed, described from a museum's or archive's page: one story, two designs; how a costume shows a character and a cultural view, checked against Holder's own words.
note: Sensitivity: the agent reads a museum's or public archive's page on Holder's designs and his own published words first; no student dresses as a real people. Holder's designs are described, never copied. Words: culture, view.

goal: Sketch drill: three quick labeled sketches for three settings of the tale, with feedback after each.
note: Baseline look on the main look-for: design ideas that suit the setting.

goal: Making steps shown with the step card: a costume piece from one fabric scrap and tape, and a set model from a folded card.
note: Equipment: scrap fabric, tape, cereal-box card, blunt scissors. Safe use: blunt scissors only, tape not pins, costume pieces loose and quick to remove, nothing tied round the neck; supplies labeled non-toxic; hands washed after glue; set models stay on the floor, never stood on. Making session: 6 minutes for clean-up. Free path: old shirts, chairs as a set.

goal: Groups choose a scene of the Oz retelling, sketch costume, prop and set ideas for it, and fill each student's character box with a look, a prop and a costume piece and the source line behind it.
note: Character boxes are for the students' own invented characters; no costume of a real group. Shorter path (spare fold-in day): folds into day 39, as a 15-minute segment.

goal: Study Roadside Theater (Whitesburg, Kentucky, founded 1975), an Appalachian company that makes plays from its own community's stories, from its own pages; the two-ties card taught with three labeled ties: community life, a social problem and another subject.
note: Sensitivity: Roadside Theater's own pages read first. Words: community, social problem, subject.

goal: Making a short piece from what the students know and have lived to connect with a community (the school's, the town's, or an invented town's), shown in steps: a small public problem, a want, a place.
note: Social problems are ones a child can name in a school or town (litter, a crowded bus, a closed playground), never a family's trouble; the invented town is marked the same; no student speaks for a whole group. Health's steps "If a student tells you something" on the teacher page. Shorter path (spare fold-in day): folds into day 41, as a 15-minute segment.

goal: Warm-up, then the opening beat of a community scene run three times with feedback.
note: Shorter path (named fold-in day, a year 10 school days short): folds into day 44, as the opener.

goal: Groups build their community scene, choosing costume pieces and set from their sketches, and fill the two-ties card.
Rehearsal with the costume piece and prop in hand, polishing one design choice so it reads in the run.
note: Words: polish. Shorter path (named fold-in day, a year 10 school days short): folds into day 46, inside the making session.

goal: Making session: groups finish costume pieces and set models to their sketches, then a short run with them.
note: Same making safety as the making-steps day; 6 minutes for clean-up.

goal: Rehearsal with the unit's one critique, led by the teacher (describe, ask, suggest) and tied to the look-fors.
Revision: groups rework from the critique; then, in the last 10 minutes, one tech element of the class's own production set beside Holder's described design for The Wiz.
note: Denslow's pictures stay background, not one of the two compared.

goal: Last rehearsal: a dress run; each student completes the prop-sketch with its character box and source line, and the two-ties card.
note: Kept sheets scored after the written day.

goal: Showing day: each group's community scene in its costume pieces and set, for a partner class, marked live on the guide.
note: Look-fors: the scene draws on a community the students know, or the invented town (Cn10.1.3a); the polished design choice used in the run (Cr3.1.3c). Partner class as audience. A group the teacher cannot watch live is recorded on the school device that day (hands, props and sound only where the family said no to faces) and marked before the respond day. Response time: the respond day after the written day, counted once.

goal: Written day: three tech elements the unseen scene could use, and one tech element compared between Holder's design and the class's own production; the prop-sketch and two-ties card are collected.
note: Written day: set-up 3, the teacher performs the unseen Curio Class scene twice (6), response card (15, at most two written items; a student may answer aloud at the table, marked the same), kept cards collected and the one-line portfolio reflection (5), close 4. Items: Pr5.1.3b and Re9.1.3b written; Cr1.1.3b the kept prop-sketch, Re8.1.3b its character box scored with it, Cn11.1.3a the kept two-ties card. Portfolio piece: the design sketch.

goal: Respond: a second try at the part marked "not yet" (a design choice made to read, a tie made clear) and a re-run for one other group.
note: Groups from the record sheet, at most four; the rest work in pairs from the written move. Starts from marks already made; no first-time evidence is collected.

goal: Year 3 year-end check: a fresh two-line scene played after one rehearsal run, marked live, a reflection card kept after the run (one line alone, one agreed with the group), and an audience card filled while another group plays; items drawn from units 1 and 2, not from unit 3 just assessed.
note: Check day: set-up 3, warm-up 3, the groups read the new card, plan and rehearse (8), each student completes the record the card names (4), six group slots of 3 minutes, each performance at most 2 minutes (18), close 4. The teacher marks one group at a time and reads the cards after the session; no artifact is scored twice. Marked live: body and voice explored for the character (Cr3.1.3b, unit 2); kept reflection card, one line alone and one agreed with the group, as the unit 1 log page does (Pr6.1.3a, unit 1); audience card on connecting with a character's feeling (Re8.1.3c, unit 2). Unit 3's record (days 50 and 51) carried unscored; unit 4 is assessed by its own showing. Week 27. Two-week rule (lead call 6, 2026-11-26): the check follows the unit's showing, but it is a showing on earlier-unit work from a fresh card with its own items, so no item repeats inside two weeks.

goal: Respond to the year-end check: a second try at the part marked "not yet", in groups from the record sheet.
note: Groups from the record sheet, at most four; the rest work in pairs from the written move. Starts from marks already made; no first-time evidence is collected.

goal: Hook: the teacher tells The Bremen Town Musicians in Curio Class's retelling of the Grimms' tale; pose the compelling question; how a written story is reshaped for the stage: what is cut, what becomes action, what becomes a line.
note: The Grimms' 1819 edition, public domain, retold by Curio Class. Words: retell, adapt, convention. Safe use: clear floor with room for arms out, chairs and bags to the walls, bare feet or soft soles.

goal: Opener retrieval with its reteach; then the parts of dramatic structure (beginning, problem, climb, end) on the story map, and the tale cut into three scenes with a freeze-frame climax.
note: Retrieval (10 minutes): a story map with a "because" arrow (th-g2-story) and one character's problem told from the audience's seat (th-g2-notice), last used in grade 2; reteach as written. Lean: RL.3.3 (how a character's actions move the story), taught in ELA grade 3 unit 1 (weeks 1 to 8), so it is used, not retaught; the "because" arrows carry it. Words: structure, beginning, middle, end.

goal: How artists of the past retold one story in other forms: the Grimms' book, Gerhard Marcks's bronze statue in Bremen (1953), and the griots of the Mande peoples, who retell long stories from memory with music and change each telling for its audience.
note: Sensitivity: griots and the Sosso-Bala (the balafon kept by one griot family in Guinea, on UNESCO's list since 2008) are studied by hearing and looking only, from UNESCO's page and a griot practitioner's own published words (the kept Candidate, 10 minutes, credited); no student imitates a griot's music or titles; the balafon's sacred keeping is named plainly. Statue described and linked.

goal: Warm-up, then the three scenes and the freeze-frame climax run three times in groups of five with feedback after each run; in the last 5 minutes each student completes the story map (one part of the tale and what it became on stage), revisable on day 60 before it is collected.
note: Baseline look on the main look-for: a clear beginning, problem and end. The robbers are chased off by noise played by the teacher or by chairs, never by a student; no student plays being hurt.

goal: Why and how groups judge a drama (an audience, a class, a festival panel), the class criteria card made together, and judging a character's problem from the audience's seat.
note: Judging is of the work, never of the maker. Words: judge, audience, situation.

goal: Rehearsal with the unit's one critique (describe, ask, suggest, led by the teacher, judged against the class criteria card), then the revision in the second half; each student revises the story map completed on day 58 where the critique changed it, and completes the criteria card.
note: Critique and revision share this day (the unit has 10 days); the story map was completed at the end of day 58, so the day holds the critique, the revision and the criteria card only. Kept story map and criteria card scored after the written day.

goal: Showing day: each group of five plays the whole short play for the class, marked live on the guide; the audience judges with the criteria card.
note: Look-for: the group's play has a clear beginning, problem and end (Pr4.1.3a). A group the teacher cannot watch live is recorded on the school device that day (hands, props and sound only where the family said no to faces) and marked before the respond day. Response time: the respond day after the written day, counted once.

goal: Written day: one way a past artist retold the tale differently from the Grimms' book, and the problem a character in the unseen scene faces, judged from the audience's seat with a reason; the story map and criteria card are collected.
note: Written day: set-up 3, the teacher performs the unseen Curio Class scene twice (6), response card (15, at most two written items; a student may answer aloud at the table, marked the same), kept cards collected and the one-line portfolio reflection (5), close 4. Items: Cn11.2.3b and Re9.1.3c written; Cn11.2.3a the kept story map; Re9.1.3a the kept criteria card. Portfolio piece: the story map.

goal: Respond: a second try at the part marked "not yet" and a re-rehearsal of the play before the family showing.
note: Groups from the record sheet, at most four; the rest work in pairs from the written move. Starts from marks already made; no first-time evidence is collected.

goal: Family showing: the class play of The Bremen Town Musicians for families, the year's costume pieces and warm-ups in use.
note: Not scored: the showing day already marked the play. Family yes for a showing outside class; a recorded or solo version is offered. Only Curio Class retellings are performed.

goal: Hook: one line played three times, at night, in a storm and late for school; pose the compelling question; Konstantin Stanislavski's "given circumstances" (who, where, when, what has happened), from a public domain source, and how an imagined world looks.
note: Kept Candidate (no day cost): the unit plan checks the Stanislavski wording against a public domain English source before it is used. Words: given circumstances, world. Safe use: clear floor with room for arms out, chairs and bags to the walls, bare feet or soft soles.

goal: Opener retrieval with its reteach; then the given-circumstances card shown in steps (who, where, when, what I want) and an improvised story fitted to it.
note: Retrieval (10 minutes): inventing by improvising from the what-if list (th-g3-imagine) and rehearse-then-reflect on the rehearsal-log (th-g3-show), last used in year 3; reteach for a student who meets year 4 first.

goal: Picturing how a character moves to fit the given circumstances: a walk at night, in a storm, late for school, shown in steps.
note: Words: invent, plot. Shorter path (spare fold-in day): folds into day 68, as a 15-minute segment of the fluency day that runs the walk.

goal: Warm-up, then the circumstances walk changed three ways in groups, with feedback after each.
note: Baseline look on the main look-for: a character who moves to fit who, where and when.

goal: The hot seat shown in steps: one student in role as an invented character, the group asks questions about the character and the plot, and the answers give new ideas on the hot-seat sheet.
note: The student in role answers as an invented character, never as themself, and may pass. Words: question.

goal: Groups improvise a scene from a new given-circumstances card, using hot-seat questions for ideas, each student choosing a role.
note: Shorter path (named fold-in day, a year 10 school days short): folds into day 69, as a 15-minute segment.

goal: Study wayang kulit, the shadow puppet theater of Indonesia, by looking only: the dalang voices every character, moves every puppet and leads the musicians; from that, the jobs a showing needs (director, stage manager, actors, sound, props, house manager).
note: Sensitivity: wayang tells Mahabharata and Ramayana stories and is played at ceremonies; studied from UNESCO's page and an Indonesian cultural body's page read first by the agent; no student makes or moves a wayang figure or imitates the dalang's voice. Words: job.

goal: Groups decide together and list the jobs their scene needs, each student takes one, and the scene runs once with its jobs.
note: The director's job never includes touching actors; stage managers call "freeze" for safety. A student who does not want to perform takes a job. Shorter path (spare fold-in day): folds into day 71, as a 15-minute segment.

goal: The run, review, rerun cycle and the critique-protocol card (describe, ask, suggest) shown in steps so the students run the critique themselves in small groups.
note: The critique-protocol model starts here. Words: revise, review.

goal: Warm-up, then the run, review, rerun cycle practiced on one scene beat three times, with the card in hand.
note: Shorter path (named fold-in day, a year 10 school days short): folds into day 75, as the opener.

goal: Rehearsal run by each group's stage manager, shown to one other group as audience.
note: Words: audience, small group.

goal: Rehearsal with the unit's one critique, run by the students with the critique-protocol card in small groups, each point tied to a look-for.
note: The teacher marks look-fors on the record sheet.

goal: Revision and last rehearsal: groups rerun from the critique; each student completes the rehearsal-log page (what changed between runs and which critique point caused it), the jobs list and the hot-seat sheet.
note: Kept pages scored after the written day.

goal: Showing day: each group's given-circumstances scene shown to classmates as audience, run by its own stage manager, marked live on the guide.
note: Look-fors: the student's character moves to fit who, where and when (Cr1.1.4c); the group's work shown to the class as audience, each student in place (Pr6.1.4a). A group the teacher cannot watch live is recorded on the school device that day (hands, props and sound only where the family said no to faces) and marked before the respond day. Response time: the respond day after the written day, counted once.

goal: Written day: how the unseen scene's world looks and how its story fits its given circumstances; the rehearsal-log page, jobs list and hot-seat sheet are collected.
note: Written day: set-up 3, the teacher performs the unseen Curio Class scene twice (6), response card (15, at most two written items; a student may answer aloud at the table, marked the same), kept cards collected and the one-line portfolio reflection (5), close 4. Items: Cr1.1.4a written (one prompt on the world, one on the fit); Cr3.1.4a the kept log page; Cr2.1.4b the kept jobs list; Cr2.1.4a the kept hot-seat sheet. Portfolio piece: the given-circumstances card with the log page.

goal: Respond: a second try at the part marked "not yet" (a walk fitted, a job carried out) and a re-run for one other group.
note: Groups from the record sheet, at most four; the rest work in pairs from the written move. Starts from marks already made; no first-time evidence is collected.

goal: Hook: the Tramp's walk from Charlie Chaplin's The Gold Rush (1925 release), from an archive's copy or stills; pose the compelling question; spotting the choices an artist made, with the film's setting; connecting (practiced, no id claimed): the Tramp in 1925 and who laughed at him.
note: Public domain in the United States in its 1925 release; a restored copy or added score carries its own rights line. The unit studies the walk and the comedy, never poverty as a joke. Paper path: printed stills. Words: choice, character. Safe use: clear floor with room for arms out, chairs and bags to the walls, bare feet or soft soles.

goal: Opener retrieval with its reteach; then the three-centers walk shown in steps (led by the nose, the knees, the chest; posture high and low).
note: Retrieval (10 minutes): the three exercise sets (th-g3-actor) and the reasons behind artists' decisions (th-g3-notice), last used in year 3; reteach as needed. No student plays a disability by its walk. Words: posture.

goal: Ensemble exercises shown in steps (the mirror, the group walk, the machine); each student chooses one to practice as a technique.

goal: Warm-up, then the scene's opening beat run with its cues three times with feedback.
note: Shorter path (named fold-in day, a year 10 school days short): folds into day 174, as the opener.

goal: Rehearsal with tech: problems found in the run and a fresh fix invented by each student for one of them.
note: Words: fix.

goal: Rehearsal with the unit's one critique, run by the students with the critique-protocol card.
Revision: groups rework from the critique, then check how their sign or cue expresses the scene's theme.
Last rehearsal: a tech run; each student completes the prop-sketch, the rehearsal-log page (the problem and the fix), the investigation sheet and the two-ties card.
note: Kept sheets scored after the written day.

goal: Showing day: each group's scene on a problem, run from its cue sheet, for a partner class, marked live on the guide.
note: Look-fors: the student runs or shows the cue as the cue sheet says (Pr5.1.5b); the scene gives a voice to the problem on the investigation sheet (Cn11.1.5a). A group the teacher cannot watch live is recorded on the school device that day (hands, props and sound only where the family said no to faces) and marked before the respond day. Response time: the respond day after the written day, counted once.

goal: Written day: how one tech element expresses a work's theme, and how a cultural view shapes a response to a character in the unseen scene; the investigation sheet, prop-sketch, log page and two-ties card are collected.
codes: TH:Re9.1.5b; TH:Re8.1.5b; TH:Cn11.1.5a; TH:Cr1.1.5b; TH:Cr3.1.5c; TH:Cn10.1.5a
note: Written day: set-up 3, the teacher performs the unseen Curio Class scene twice (6), response card (15, at most two written items; a student may answer aloud at the table, marked the same), kept cards collected and the one-line portfolio reflection (5), close 4. Items: Re9.1.5b and Re8.1.5b written; Cn11.1.5a the kept investigation sheet (three context fields); Cr1.1.5b the kept prop-sketch; Cr3.1.5c the kept log page; Cn10.1.5a the kept two-ties card. Portfolio piece: the cue sheet.

goal: Respond: a second try at the part marked "not yet" (a cue on time, a problem given a clearer voice) and a re-run for one other group.
note: Groups from the record sheet, at most four; the rest work in pairs from the written move. Starts from marks already made; no first-time evidence is collected.

goal: Year 5 year-end check: a fresh scene from a new card, marked live, a self-review line written after the first rehearsal run inside the 8 planning minutes, naming the change made in the rerun, and an audience card defending a reaction to another group's choice; items drawn from units 9 and 10, not from unit 11 just assessed.
note: Check day: set-up 3, warm-up 3, the groups read the new card, plan and rehearse (8), each student completes the record the card names (4), six group slots of 3 minutes, each performance at most 2 minutes (18), close 4. The teacher marks one group at a time and reads the cards after the session; no artifact is scored twice. Marked live: a physical choice that carries meaning (Pr4.1.5b, unit 10) and body and voice that build the character (Cr3.1.5b, unit 10); kept self-review line, written after the first rehearsal run inside the 8 planning minutes and naming the change made in the rerun (Cr3.1.5a, unit 9: repeating and self-reviewing); audience card with a reaction defended by an experience (Re8.1.5a, unit 10). Unit 11's record (days 178 and 179) carried unscored; unit 12 is assessed by its own showing. Week 27. Two-week rule (lead call 6, 2026-11-26): the check follows the unit's showing, but it is a showing on earlier-unit work from a fresh card with its own items, so no item repeats inside two weeks.

goal: Respond to the year-end check: a second try at the part marked "not yet", in groups from the record sheet.
note: Groups from the record sheet, at most four; the rest work in pairs from the written move. Starts from marks already made; no first-time evidence is collected.

goal: Hook: a paper fish-bone cutout and a slipper on a chair; pose the compelling question; three Cinderella tellings in Curio Class's retellings (Ye Xian, China, about 850; Charles Perrault's Cendrillon, France, 1697; the Poor Turkey Girl of Zuni Pueblo, read for comparison only), compared for what they share and what is their own on the comparison chart.
note: Sensitivity: the Poor Turkey Girl is used only if the Zuni Pueblo's own museum and heritage pages treat it as open to be told, read and compared only, never acted; otherwise the kept swap pool (the Candidate) gives another culture's telling with the ids kept. Stepfamily cruelty told plainly, played by an object or the teacher. Lean: RL.5.3, taught in ELA grade 5 unit 1 (weeks 1 to 9); the chart gives the tellings' characters and events in rows. Words: compare, version. Safe use: clear floor with room for arms out, chairs and bags to the walls, bare feet or soft soles. The fish bone is a paper cutout (props rule: nothing sharp or small enough to swallow).

goal: Opener retrieval with its reteach; then the hidden-thought line under each spoken line shown in steps (the thought, the feeling with it, the line or action it drives), and groups choose the Perrault or the Ye Xian telling for their play.
note: Retrieval (10 minutes): a rewritten ending (th-g4-story) and an offered way of judging (th-g4-judge), last used in year 4. No student is asked about their own family. Words: motive, hidden.

goal: Shakespeare's First Folio (London, 1623) in a library's open copy: the stage directions of The Tempest ("Enter", "Exit", "Exeunt" and an aside) as the old source for stage terms and customs; groups put one term and one convention into their scripts with hidden-thought lines.
note: A named maker revisit from unit 9, with a new work and a new job. Paper path: the printed First Folio page. Words: source, custom, term.

goal: Warm-up, then each group's scenes run three times with the hidden thought made readable in the acting, with feedback after each run; in the last 5 minutes each student completes the script annotation (the hidden thought under two of the character's lines), revisable on day 188 before it is collected.
note: Baseline look on the main look-for: a line played with its hidden thought readable.

goal: Making a judging guide with the class, and seeing how a character's situation changes how the audience views the piece (the girl's situation in each telling).
note: Judging is of the work, never of the maker. Words: guide, situation, judge.

goal: Rehearsal with the unit's one critique, run by the students with the critique-protocol card and the class judging guide, then the revision in the second half; each student revises the script annotation completed on day 186 where the critique changed it, and completes the script page with its term and convention.
note: Critique and revision share this day (the unit has 10 days); the script annotation was completed at the end of day 186, so the day holds the critique, the revision and the script page only. Kept script pages scored after the written day.

goal: Showing day: each group's short play with First Folio stage directions, for the class, marked live; each student marks another group's play on the class judging guide.
note: Look-for: the student's line played with its hidden thought readable (Pr4.1.5a, with the kept annotation). Kept: the judging guide with the student's marks (Re9.1.5a). Only the Perrault or Ye Xian retelling is performed. A group the teacher cannot watch live is recorded on the school device that day (hands, props and sound only where the family said no to faces) and marked before the respond day. Response time: the respond day after the written day, counted once.

goal: Written day: one trait the three tellings share and one that belongs to one culture's telling, and how a character's situation in the unseen scene changes how the student views the piece; the script annotation and script page are collected.
note: Written day: set-up 3, the teacher performs the unseen Curio Class scene twice (6), response card (15, at most two written items; a student may answer aloud at the table, marked the same), kept cards collected and the one-line portfolio reflection (5), close 4. Items: Cn11.2.5a (a prompt for the shared trait, one for the trait of its own) and Re9.1.5c written; Cn11.2.5b the kept script page (term and convention, each explained from its source); Pr4.1.5a the kept annotation. Portfolio piece: the script page.

goal: Respond: a second try at the part marked "not yet" and a re-rehearsal before the family showing.
note: Groups from the record sheet, at most four; the rest work in pairs from the written move. Starts from marks already made; no first-time evidence is collected.

goal: Family showing: each group's short play from the Perrault or Ye Xian retelling, with First Folio stage directions, for families; the band closes.
note: Not scored: the showing day already marked the plays. The Poor Turkey Girl is never part of the family showing. Family yes for a showing outside class; a recorded or solo version is offered.
